rv.q: The Glitch is resoundingly clear in its testament to the power of theater to interrogate our technological anxieties with grace, wit, and emotional intelligence.
The Glitch never finds its footing in either conception or execution.
Having no arms is an annoyance, but having no place on the stage is a glitch in need of a fix.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this sci-fi romance about tech-assisted parenthood, with praise for its provocative premise but sharp criticism of its tonal confusion and execution as an awkward "dramatic farce."
